note: Imported by tools/import_headwear_green.py from a sheet whose person was painted flat #00FF00. The hat is simply everything that is neither the magenta backdrop nor the green person, so no head can leak into the frame and no colour heuristic can eat a hat pixel. Checked against the iris row the game paints (eyeMask.json). v2.3.2361: north omitted on purpose -- the eyewear is not visible from there. At -14 the lens sat almost entirely inside the face, immediately beside the near eye, which is exactly the 'middle of the face' reading.  The SOUTH facing is the one the owner is happy with and it hangs roughly HALF the lens past the head's left silhouette; -22 reproduces that proportion in the 3/4 view. Chosen from a rendered sweep of -14/-18/-22/-26 against the south cell as the reference, not from arithmetic: two attempts to compute the overhang analytically both went wrong, once by re-implementing _placeTrait by hand (the very thing preview_headwear.py's header warns is a second opinion rather than a check) and once by measuring the skull's widest point instead of the face at the eye row.  -26 was too far: the lens leaves the eye and the piece reads as floating beside the head rather than clamped on it.
